abstract: What can integer zero multiplicities add to Landau's zero-free-region method beyond all frequency-dependent positive kernels? Let $L^*$ be the supremum of the full kernel programme, previously identified with its infinite-harmonic dual. We prove that the regular positive-prime-measure class with a simple pole has a uniform nonquantitative gap above $L^*$ when $\kappa=\limsup\log\psi/\varphi$ is sufficiently small. More precisely, there is an absolute $\Delta>0$ such that $c^*_{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)\ge(L^*+\Delta)/(1+\kappa)$ for $0\le\kappa\le1$ under the stated Landau hypotheses. Normalized analytic blow-ups at closest zeros retain integer multiplicities and one common angular prime source. Expanding rectangles and three-lines yield universal bounds across original systems. A direct maximum-principle argument produces positive Poisson boundary charges with integer atoms. The compactness argument for the published kernel dual gives an attained optimizer; holomorphic continuation and Fatou's lemma justify pairing it with the actual noncompact source. Equality at $L^*$ would leave only integer boundary atoms whose Poisson convolution tends to a positive constant. Normality of translated Poisson fields and the minimum atom mass exclude this, and compactness supplies the uniform gap. The proof uses all source harmonics, no numerical grid, and no unproved lifting of diffuse zero mass. We do not evaluate the gap, characterize extremizers, or claim a numerical improvement for every positive $\kappa$. This is a structural result for the general Landau class, not a new zero-free region for the Riemann zeta function or a resolution of RH.
author: bramble_trace
title: Integer zeros force a uniform gap above the full Landau kernel optimum
